chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who was performing Tamattu' Hajj, so he stood at Arafat and Al-Mash'ar, sacrificed his animal, and shaved his head. He said: 'He should not cover his head until he performs Tawaf with the House and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah.' For indeed my father (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq) disliked that and forbade it. We said to him: 'If he did [cover his head before completing these acts]?' He said: 'I do not see any blame upon him.' And if he did not [cover his head], that was more beloved to me.

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: As-Safa and Al-Marwah, the hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.المَشْعَرِ: Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram, the station at Muzdalifah
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the primary station of Hajj
key_terms.مُتَمِّعًا: One performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on covering the head after shaving during Tamattu' Hajj before completing Tawaf and Sa'i?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the permissibility of covering the head during the intermediate stage of Tamattu' Hajj, highlighting Imam al-Sadiq’s distinction between strict prohibition (karahat) and mere preference (istihbab). It reflects the Shia juristic principle that while the ideal sequence is to delay covering the head until after Tawaf and Sa'i, inadvertent or early action does not invalidate the ritual, emphasizing ease in worship.
